evidence: The load-bearing premise that no later-closure policy exists fails when the named spec's reuse contracts are read together. The whole spec says to 'Reuse existing open-item resolution' (line 60), identifies the existing ledger/fold/validator under src/summary/ as its baseline (line 19), and defines that reuse as 'using existing Resolved status and transition validation' (line 102). It also requires daemon status validity (line 104) and sequence-ordered final folding (lines 70 and 108). The existing fold's equivalent mechanism is an explicit still-open guard: src/summary/fold.rs:49–55 specifies dropping a transition with a reason when its target is no longer open; lines 100–101 enforce that guard and line 120 records the drop without failing the fold. The existing regression example at lines 407–431 verifies that the second closure drops as 'target not open', preserves the first closure's status/citation, and reports the drop. Thus the concurrent fetched-snapshot scenario is possible, but it does not require transition deduplication or a new policy: the earliest sequence-ordered valid closure applies, and the later closure is dropped by the reused status guard. The named spec changes kind eligibility and event ordering without removing that guard. Treating the later transition as an unspecified cover failure overlooks an existing mechanism expressly reused by the named design.
